articles.title: What If Justin Gaethje BEATS Arman Tsarukyan?
articles.description: What happens if Justin Gaethje beats Arman Tsarukyan? Gaethje has openly said he's deciding between another fight and retirement, and if he does fight again, Arman appears to be the opponent. But once again, the MMA community is preparing to count Gaethje out. We do this every time. Gaethje was doubted against Rafael Fiziev. He was doubted going into an interim title fight. And if he faces Arman, he'll likely be the underdog again. But what if he wins? Does Gaethje take another fight? Does he walk away on top? And what would beating Arman at this stage do for his legacy? Alexander Volkanovski has also publicly called Gaethje out and Gaethje's lack of response might be telling us something about where his head is right now. Whatever Gaethje decides, Chael Sonnen believes the community should make one thing clear: it's okay. Fight Arman, fight Volk, or walk away. He's earned the right to choose. #JustinGaethje #ArmanTsarukyan #UFC #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: Justin Gaethje Should Be Paying Attention #ufc
articles.description: Alexander Volkanovski has opened the door for a potential lightweight fight with Justin Gaethje. So why hasn't Gaethje said anything? Chael Sonnen believes this is a major opportunity for Justin. He explains why the UFC's leadership—including Dana White, Hunter Campbell, and Sean Shelby—may not be interested in making the matchup. But that could actually create an opening for Gaethje to push the situation in his favor. Volkanovski has made his intentions public. The matchup is there to be discussed, and Chael thinks Gaethje has a chance to take advantage of the situation. But so far, Justin hasn't taken the shot. He hasn't accepted the callout, and he hasn't publicly responded. Chael admits he doesn't know how to interpret the silence. Is Gaethje waiting for the right opportunity, or is he passing on a fight that could change everything? #ChaelSonnen #JustinGaethje #AlexanderVolkanovski #UFC #MMA #UFCNews

articles.title: Ciryl Gane Is NOT a Cheater
articles.description: Use my code CHAEL to get up to 50% off your Hume Pod: https://sponsr.is/humehealth_chael Is Ciryl Gane a cheater because of the eye poke that ended his fight with Tom Aspinall? Dominick Cruz and TJ Dillashaw recently discussed the question, and Chael Sonnen is weighing in. His answer is clear: Ciryl Gane is not a cheater. Gane broke a rule, but Chael believes the important distinction is intent. There's a difference between an accidental foul and deliberately trying to gain an advantage by breaking the rules. Chael sees no reason to believe Gane intentionally tried to poke Aspinall in the eye. But that raises a bigger question: should intent determine the punishment? Chael looks at how MMA handles accidental eye pokes, fence grabs, and other fouls, and asks whether fighters should face a more meaningful consequence even when the violation wasn't intentional. With so few fundamental rules in MMA, should breaking one of them carry a greater price? Gane isn't a cheater. But that doesn't mean the sport has the foul problem figured out. #CirylGane #TomAspinall #ChaelSonnen #UFC #MMA

articles.title: Volkanovski Could Take Arman Tsarukyan’s Title Fight #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen believes Alexander Volkanovski could be putting Arman Tsarukyan’s next title opportunity in jeopardy. Chael reveals that he sent Arman a message on WhatsApp asking if he understood what Volkanovski was attempting to do. By publicly pursuing a move to lightweight and potentially a fight with Justin Gaethje, Volk could be stepping directly into the title picture Arman has been waiting for. But there's another possibility. Chael believes Gaethje could vacate the lightweight championship, which would change the entire situation and potentially open the door for Arman. So where does that leave Tsarukyan if Volkanovski gets the fight he wants? Chael breaks down the lightweight title picture, the potential Gaethje matchup, and why Volkanovski's next move could have major consequences for Arman's championship plans. #ChaelSonnen #ArmanTsarukyan #AlexanderVolkanovski #JustinGaethje #UFC #MMA #UFCNews

articles.title: Justin Gaethje's Silence Is Getting LOUD
articles.description: Justin Gaethje isn't saying anything and Chael Sonnen thinks that silence has become incredibly powerful. Normally, one of the worst things a fighter can do is disappear. Stay relevant. Keep talking. Give people something to discuss. But Gaethje may have accidentally found the exception. Since his last fight, he's done more major media than ever, yet he's refused to answer the one question everyone wants answered: What's next? Now Alexander Volkanovski has fired two shots at Gaethje. First, he called him out. Then Volk announced he was willing to vacate the featherweight title and come after the lightweight championship. Still nothing from Gaethje. Chael doesn't believe it was some calculated strategy. But intentional or not, it's working. Every week Gaethje remains silent, the anticipation grows. And now Chael believes he has to keep it that way. Because the first time Justin Gaethje finally speaks, everybody is going to listen. #JustinGaethje #AlexanderVolkanovski #UFC #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: Alexander Volkanovski’s 7-Year Quest for the Lightweight Title
articles.description: Alexander Volkanovski has chased a second UFC belt for seven years. This is the full story of Volk’s quest to become a two-division champion, from his featherweight title win over Max Holloway to two fights with Islam Makhachev, the Ilia Topuria knockout, and his call for a lightweight super fight with Justin Gaethje after UFC 333. Before the belts, Volkanovski was a concreter from Wollongong, Australia, who played rugby league at as much as 214 pounds. He cut down to featherweight, went unbeaten in the UFC on the way to a title shot, and started looking up at lightweight in 2021. He lost to Makhachev twice in 2023, lost his featherweight title to Topuria in 2024, then came back to beat Diego Lopes twice and finish the undefeated Movsar Evloev. Now, he says, a fight with Gaethje is “something I would retire for.” Told in Volk’s own words, with Dana White, from MMA Weekly’s press conferences, media days and weigh-ins, 2019 to 2026. Should the UFC give Volkanovski his shot at the lightweight title? Tell us in the comments. articles.title: I feel like Chimaev agreed with me #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen thought Khamzat Chimaev might be reaching for a weapon. Turns out, it was nothing like that. Chael tells a hilarious story about an encounter with Khamzat, who at the time didn't have a beard. Chael tells him to stop, and Khamzat immediately pulls up his pant leg and starts reaching toward his sock. For a moment, Chael doesn't know what he's about to pull out. Is it a holster? A knife? Something else? But the explanation is much simpler—and a lot funnier. Khamzat was wearing a slip-on Vans shoe that had come off, and he was just trying to get his foot back inside. Even Chael has to laugh at the misunderstanding. He says Khamzat seemed to understand why he told him to stop. A funny behind-the-scenes Khamzat Chimaev story from Chael Sonnen. #ChaelSonnen #KhamzatChimaev #UFC #MMA #UFCStories #MMAStories

articles.title: Jake Paul has a date and location but no opponent
articles.description: Jake Paul has a date. He has a location. What he apparently doesn't have yet is an opponent. Chael Sonnen doesn't believe Jake can necessarily go wrong with the choice, but the list of possibilities is getting interesting. Francis Ngannou remains a possibility after Jake previously called him out. Nate Diaz is expected to participate on the Abu Dhabi card, although Chael doesn't believe that necessarily means he'll face Jake. Mike Perry could also be involved, but Jake has already competed against both men. Then there are the elite boxers. Chael doesn't expect Jake to go that direction either. So who's left? If Jake's opponent were already locked in, Chael believes we probably would have heard the name with the announcement. That means the search may still be happening and the reaction from the fans could matter. Jake Paul is fighting in Abu Dhabi on Christmas Eve. Who do you want standing across from him? #JakePaul #Boxing #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: Money Moicano Made a BIG Mistake
articles.description: Renato Moicano says he wants to fight out his UFC contract. Chael Sonnen thinks saying that publicly was a mistake. If your goal is to reach the end of your contract, the first rule should be simple: don't tell the promoter that's what you're planning to do. Moicano has built himself into one of MMA's most interesting personalities. He's headlining this weekend, getting the press conference spotlight, and the UFC keeps investing promotional resources in him because people want to hear what he has to say. But now he's 37, he's an underdog against Tom Nolan, and he's publicly announced that he intends to fight out his deal. That changes the equation. Why would the UFC continue giving Moicano main events and promotional opportunities if it believes he's preparing to leave? Talking helped Moicano get here. Chael just hopes talking doesn't cost him the very opportunities he worked so hard to earn. #RenatoMoicano #MoneyMoicano #UFC #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: Volkanovski Finally Had a GOOD Idea
articles.description: Alexander Volkanovski finally came up with an idea Chael Sonnen loves. Vacate the featherweight championship. Move to 155 pounds. And fight Arman Tsarukyan. Volkanovski originally called out Justin Gaethje, but there was a problem: that fight would effectively take away the opportunity Arman had already earned. Now Volk has changed the proposal. If Gaethje walks away from the sport and the lightweight championship becomes vacant, Volkanovski wants Arman. Chael loves it. Volk gets the challenge he says he wants. Arman gets the championship opportunity he earned. And featherweight can move forward with contenders like Aljamain Sterling and Jean Silva competing for the vacant belt. There may also be something else behind Volk's announcement. Chael believes Volkanovski is hearing the same whispers around the sport that everyone else is starting to hear: Justin Gaethje may be much closer to retirement than 50-50. Whatever prompted it, Chael is sold. Volkanovski vs. Tsarukyan is the best idea Volk has offered yet. #AlexanderVolkanovski #ArmanTsarukyan #JustinGaethje #UFC #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: There Is NO Debate: O'Malley vs. Yan Is Next
articles.description: Sean O'Malley says there is no debate and no argument: the Petr Yan rematch is next. Chael Sonnen agrees. What makes O'Malley's statement so powerful is that he almost never does this. Throughout his rise, Sean accepted fights that Chael didn't always understand, went out and did his job, and rarely demanded a specific opponent. Now he's finally playing that card. Petr Yan has every right to take his time after reclaiming the championship, but Chael believes Yan will eventually say yes. He's a competitor first, and a rematch with O'Malley gives him exactly the kind of challenge that has defined his career. If O'Malley can get Yan to publicly agree, the UFC has a very easy decision to make. They have history. They have unfinished business. And now O'Malley has finally spoken up. There is no debate. There is no argument. O'Malley vs. Yan 2 is next. #SeanOMalley #PetrYan #UFC #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: There’s Nobody for Khamzat Chimaev to Fight
articles.description: Use my code CHAEL to get up to 50% off your Hume Pod: https://sponsr.is/humehealth_chael He has separated himself from the rest of the middleweight division. After what he did to Robert Whittaker and Dricus Du Plessis, I don’t think you can responsibly throw him in there with the No. 8 or No. 9 guy just to keep him busy. Khamzat is that good. So does he wait? Normally, I hate that idea. But with Sean Strickland and Nassourdine Imavov matched up, I’m not sure there’s a better option. Let Strickland and Imavov settle it, then put Khamzat in there with the winner. He’s clearly next. articles.title: What is Volkanovski thinking? #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen thinks Alexander Volkanovski has come up with one of the dumbest ideas he’s ever heard. Volkanovski’s idea of moving to 155 pounds to test himself raises one big question for Chael: what does a fight with Justin Gaethje actually accomplish? Chael doesn’t see who benefits from that matchup, especially when Volkanovski could make a much bigger statement by fully committing to the lightweight division. If Volk really wants to test himself, Chael argues, he should be willing to drop the belt and go all in. He points to Ilia Topuria as the example of a fighter willing to make a major move rather than simply talk about taking on a new challenge. Chael makes his position clear: being a great fighter doesn’t require being a great promoter. If Volkanovski wants to prove himself at lightweight, Chael believes he needs to make the commitment. Is Volk’s idea a smart move—or does Chael have a point? Subscribe for more Chael Sonnen analysis, UFC news, and MMA breakdowns. #ChaelSonnen #AlexanderVolkanovski #JustinGaethje #IliaTopuria #UFC #MMA

articles.title: Sean O'Malley REACTS to DC's Song Yadong CALLOUT after Petr Yan win, Payton Talbott | Daniel Cormier
articles.description: DC IS BACK with another special edition of the Daniel Cormier Show, this time talking to the number-one contender in the UFC's bantamweight division, Sean O'Malley, after Petr Yan defended his championship against Merab Dvalishvili in Abu Dhabi. Cormier talks to Sean about calling out Song Yadong in the arena after Yan's win, and about O'Malley's live reaction to that moment. DC says that it was because Song was there that he called for him in that moment, but still believes Sean is the top contender in the division. O'Malley and DC talk about why he's next to fight Yan, why he was ready to fight Payton Talbott next if Merab happened to take the title back, and what makes Sean such an incredible fighter in the sport.
